headline: Doets wins ten legs in a row to beat Wattimena 16-7
standfirst: Kevin Doets reached the first major semi-final we have on record for him, and Jermaine Wattimena averaged 100.06 in defeat.
body: Kevin Doets has reached the first major semi-final we have on record for him, beating fellow Dutchman Jermaine Wattimena 16-7 in the Grand Slam of Darts quarter-finals in Wolverhampton on Friday. It was a match that was level at 5-5, then turned into a one-sided one: Doets won the next ten legs without reply.

That run is the story of the night. From 5-5 he took every leg of the third session, including a 170 checkout in leg 14 and a second 170, this time in 12 darts, in leg 19. Wattimena, who had the better of the early exchanges and led 5-4, did not win another leg until the score was 14-5.

The numbers say it was closer than the scoreline. Doets averaged 102.63, against 96.44 over his last 12 months, but Wattimena averaged 100.06, up from 94.71 over the same period, and checked out at 53.9 per cent to Doets’ 45.7. That 100.06 is the highest losing average of this event. Doets simply broke throw seven times to Wattimena’s three, and the 9-leg lead he built was the biggest of the match.

The result ends a good week for Wattimena, who beat Luke Littler 10-8 in the last 16 and matched his quarter-final of 2024. Doets, ranked 23rd to Wattimena’s 18th, was making his first appearance at the event on record. The pair had met 13 times before, with Doets ahead 7-6 in those meetings.
Doets has guaranteed himself £60,000. He plays Gerwyn Price in the semi-finals on Sunday at 1:15pm, with Price having needed a deciding leg to get past Niko Springer.
